backlog.spec: In infer(), replace the tta level 2 path used by predict() with mirror-only test-time augmentation: average net(x) and net(x.flip(-1)) for all test images, dropping the translated crop views in _get_tta_logits and the 25 percent uncertain-subset selection. This cuts prediction time and should cost little accuracy. Keep the model unchanged and keep predict's signature.
backlog.title: Mirror-only TTA at prediction

backlog.spec: In tta(), set UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE to 1.0 so the flip and shifted-view averaging is applied to every test image instead of the 25 percent least confident ones. Keep the batching with tta_batch_size=2000. This spends a little more prediction time for a possible accuracy gain.
backlog.title: TTA on all test images

backlog.spec: In _get_tta_logits, extend the views beyond the current original plus two corner crops of the reflect-padded image. Add the two remaining diagonal 2-pixel crops (top-right and bottom-left) so there are five shifted views, each also flipped. Average all logits equally. Keep the rest of the pipeline and predict() unchanged.
backlog.title: Five-view TTA with diagonal shifts

backlog.spec: Set the color_jitter entry in the train() aug dict to enabled False, so batch_color_jitter is never called. This removes one compiled augmentation pass per epoch. The 7.65 epoch budget stays fixed, so accuracy may drop slightly but runtime also drops slightly.
backlog.title: Remove color jitter augmentation

backlog.spec: Replace the epoch-alternating flip in CifarLoader.__iter__ with an independent random flip for each image in every epoch, using batch_flip_lr on the batch or a per-sample torch.where on the flip mask. The current scheme flips all images together every other epoch, so per-sample flips give more diversity within each epoch.
backlog.title: Per-sample random horizontal flip

backlog.spec: Add cutout to the augmentation: for each training batch, with probability 0.5 per image, zero out a random 8x8 square of the normalised images (set to 0 after normalisation, which is the mean colour). Implement it inside a small torch.compile'd helper applied in CifarLoader.__iter__ after translation. Keep all other augmentation as is.
backlog.title: Cutout regularisation

backlog.spec: Change TRANSLATE from 2 to 3. The reflect padding in CifarLoader and the batch_crop helper already take the pad from the config, so only the constant needs changing. Also update the TTA pad in infer() from 1 to 2 so the test-time shifts match. This tests stronger translation augmentation.
backlog.title: Translation of 3 pixels

backlog.spec: Start training with batch size 512 and grow it to 1536 over the run, for example by doubling the batch at 25 and 60 percent of total steps. Recompute the CifarLoader batch size per epoch and scale the LR of all groups by the batch ratio. Keep total_train_steps consistent with the epoch count. Smaller early batches give more updates early on.
backlog.title: Progressive batch size growth

backlog.spec: CifarLoader drops the last 848 shuffled images each epoch because drop_last is True. Instead, for training, build the epoch index as a random permutation concatenated with its first few entries so the last batch is full and every image appears each epoch. Keep len(loader) consistent with the step budget, so the total number of steps does not change.
backlog.title: Wrap-padded final batch

backlog.spec: Replace the linear-to-zero decay for both optimizers with cosine decay to zero: factor = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*step/total_train_steps)). Apply it to lr_factor1 for the bias group and lr_factor2 for the Muon and head groups in train(). Muon's target magnitude decay in _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 can stay linear.
backlog.title: Cosine LR decay

backlog.spec: Add a linear warmup over the first 3 percent of total_train_steps, multiplying every group's LR by min(1, step/warmup_steps) on top of the existing linear decay. Apply it in the training loop where lr_factor1 and lr_factor2 are computed. This stabilises the early Muon updates at the high LR of 0.205.
backlog.title: Short LR warmup

backlog.spec: Keep the LR constant at its initial value for the first 60 percent of total_train_steps, then decay linearly to zero over the last 40 percent. Use this in place of the current linear-from-start decay, for both lr_factor1 and lr_factor2. The high-LR plateau may improve accuracy at the same step count.
backlog.title: Trapezoidal LR schedule

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, reduce the orthogonalisation from three quintic iterations to two. Remove the third block of A/B/X updates. This cuts Muon's per-step cost. Accuracy may change slightly, so the step budget may need a small adjustment.
backlog.title: Two Newton-Schulz iterations

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, add two more quintic iterations (A, B, X update blocks) for five in total, to make the Muon update closer to an exact orthogonal polar factor. This costs some time per step but may improve the convolution filters' optimisation quality.
backlog.title: Five Newton-Schulz iterations

backlog.spec: Move model.head.weight out of the SGD param group and into the Muon optimizer as a 2D matrix. Muon currently only collects 4D conv filters, so extend its meta-data collection in __init__ and step to treat 2D params as (D, K) with no reshape. Keep the head's own LR and weight decay settings.
backlog.title: Muon on the head weight

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA copy of the conv and head weights during the last 30 percent of training, with decay 0.999 updated once per step. At the end of train(), copy the EMA weights into the model before returning. This is done in train(), so predict() still does not modify the model. Keep the EMA buffers local to train().
backlog.title: Exponential moving average of weights for prediction

backlog.spec: Replace nn.SiLU in ConvGroup with nn.ReLU, both in the conv group activations. ReLU is cheaper and fuses more easily under torch.compile, which may cut time per step. Accuracy may drop slightly, so keep the epoch budget as is.
backlog.title: ReLU instead of SiLU

backlog.spec: In CifarNet.layers, replace the final nn.MaxPool2d(3) with adaptive average pooling to 1x1 (nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)). Keep the head and its 1/x.size(-1) scaling as is, or rescale the head output to match the new feature statistics. Average pooling may generalise better than max pooling on the 4x4 map.
backlog.title: Global average pooling instead of final max pool

backlog.spec: Change widths block1 from 64 to 48 in CifarNet's widths dict. This shrinks the first block's convolution and BN cost and should reduce runtime, with a small accuracy loss. Confirm the whiten_width and the ConvGroup input dims still match, because block2 takes block1's width.
backlog.title: Narrower first block

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.forward, remove norm1 and its call, keeping the pool, the first SiLU activation, and norm2 after conv2. Delete norm1 from the module definition. This cuts one BatchNorm pass per block. The norm-bias parameters are still picked up by the name filter in train(), so no other edit is needed.
backlog.title: Remove the first BatchNorm in each ConvGroup

backlog.spec: Add nn.Dropout(0.1) on the flattened features before self.head in CifarNet.forward. It is active only in model.train() mode, so predict() is unaffected. This is a light regulariser and may help a little at 7.65 epochs.
backlog.title: Dropout before the head

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed division by x.size(-1) in CifarNet.forward with a learnable scalar parameter initialised to 1/x.size(-1) (for example a 1-element nn.Parameter). Include it in the SGD group with the head, so the logit scale can adapt during training. Keep reset() consistent with the new parameter.
backlog.title: Learnable head output scale

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 2048 and scale the LR of the bias, head and Muon groups by sqrt(2048/1536) to keep the update size comparable. The step count drops by about 25 percent, which should reduce per-epoch overhead. Keep EPOCHS unchanged and re-derive the weight decay term, wd = WEIGHT_DECAY * batch size, from the new batch size.
backlog.title: Batch size 2048 with scaled LR

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed LABEL_SMOOTHING of 0.09 with a schedule that starts at 0.2 and linearly decays to 0.0 over total_train_steps. Set the value in forward_step through a mutable tensor or a Python float recomputed each step. Label smoothing is a regulariser that matters less near the end of short training.
backlog.title: Label smoothing schedule

backlog.spec: Change the decorator on forward_step from mode='max-autotune' to mode='reduce-overhead' so CUDA graphs cut the per-step launch overhead. Keep fullgraph=True. Also check that the whiten_bias_grad flag does not force a recompile every step, for example by making it a Python bool that switches once. This targets the per-step launch cost.
backlog.title: Reduce-overhead compile mode for the training step

backlog.spec: Remove the Python loop that sets group['lr'] for each param group every step. Store each group's LR as a 0-dim CUDA tensor and update all of them in one torch._foreach_mul_ or fill call from precomputed factors. Keep optimizer.step() calls unchanged. This removes the small host-side overhead per step.
backlog.title: Tensor-valued LR updates

backlog.spec: Change whiten_kernel_size from 2 to 3 in CifarNet, which changes the whiten width to 2*3*9 = 54 channels. The init_whiten patch code already uses h and w from the weight shape, so it adapts automatically. The larger patch whitening may capture more local structure. Check the padding and the 32 to 30 spatial size before block1.
backlog.title: Whitening kernel of size 3

backlog.spec: In predict(), deep-copy the model, recompute the BatchNorm running statistics on the test images in train-mode forward passes with momentum None (cumulative average) on the copy, then run infer on the copy. The original model is never modified, which satisfies the rule against changing it in predict. This tests whether test-set statistics help.
backlog.title: Test-time BN recalibration on a copy

backlog.spec: In train(), change the init_whiten input from train_loader.normalize(train_loader.images[:960]) to the first 5000 training images. The patch covariance is then estimated from more data. Only data from the current run is used, which is allowed. This may give a better whitening basis at negligible cost.
backlog.title: More images for whitening initialisation

backlog.spec: Ramp MUON_MOMENTUM linearly from 0.5 at step 0 up to the configured 0.655 over the first 10 percent of total_train_steps. Update group['momentum'] in optimizer2 each step inside train(), before opt.step(). Early steps then take smaller, less noisy orthogonalised updates while the momentum buffer is still filling.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: For the first 40 percent of training steps, downsample each augmented training batch from 32x32 to 28x28 with F.interpolate (bilinear, antialias=True), so early steps are cheaper. Switch to full 32x32 for the remaining steps. Keep the whitening init on full-resolution images, and keep the model unchanged: at 28x28 the spatial sizes go 27, 13, 6, 3 and the final MaxPool2d(3) still reduces to 1x1. Predict and the TTA path stay at 32x32. Everything else (LR schedules, augmentation order, batch size) stays the same.
backlog.title: Progressive resolution: train early epochs at 28x28

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.forward, add a skip connection around the second convolution: after norm1 and the first SiLU, save x as identity, then compute conv2 -> norm2 -> SiLU and return that output plus identity. The first ConvGroup has 64 channels in and 64 out after conv1, but block2 and block3 change width (64->256, 256->256), so apply the skip only when channel counts match, or use a 1x1 conv without bias for the mismatched block. Keep the BatchNorm without learned scale, and keep the Muon/SGD grouping unchanged.
backlog.title: Residual skip around conv2 in each ConvGroup

backlog.spec: In CifarNet, delete the nn.GELU() at the start of self.layers so the whitening convolution feeds straight into the first ConvGroup. This removes one nonlinearity on the whitened features and saves a small elementwise kernel. Nothing else changes: the whitening weights stay frozen, and the whiten bias keeps its warmup schedule.
backlog.title: Remove the initial GELU before the first ConvGroup

backlog.spec: Reorder ConvGroup.forward to conv1 -> norm1 -> SiLU -> max-pool 2x2 -> conv2 -> norm2 -> SiLU. Currently pooling sits between conv1 and norm1. Because SiLU is monotone-ish and the pooled max is taken on post-activation values, this changes the feature statistics seen by norm1 and the cost of the first BatchNorm, which now runs on the 4x larger pre-pool map. Keep the head, the final MaxPool2d(3), and all hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Move max pooling after the activation in each ConvGroup

backlog.spec: Replace the bias-free nn.Linear head in CifarNet with a cosine classifier. L2-normalise the 256-dim pooled features and the 10 class weight vectors, multiply the cosine scores by a learnable scalar s initialised to 10 (stored as a single parameter in the head's optimizer group with the head LR), and drop the existing head(x) / x.size(-1) scaling. The reset() method must still initialise the head weights, and predict must return the scaled cosine logits. Only the head changes.
backlog.title: Cosine-similarity head with learnable temperature

backlog.spec: Make the first ConvGroup use a single 3x3 convolution: remove conv2 and norm2 from block1 only, so the path is conv1 -> pool -> norm1 -> SiLU, and feed 64 channels into block2 as before. This halves the work in the highest-resolution stage. Blocks 2 and 3 are unchanged. The Muon filter list is built from model.parameters(), so it will pick up the smaller set automatically. Keep all hyperparameters as they are.
backlog.title: Drop the second convolution in the first block

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 1024 and scale the step-size hyperparameters by 1024/1536 (about 0.667): BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR, and MUON_LR. Recompute WEIGHT_DECAY through the existing formula, since wd = WEIGHT_DECAY * batch size. The step count rises by about 1.5x, so total_train_steps and whiten_bias_train_steps are still derived from len(train_loader). Keep EPOCHS unchanged. This tests whether more, smaller steps give better accuracy per second at this model size.
backlog.title: Batch size 1024 with linearly scaled learning rates

backlog.spec: At 50 percent of training steps, copy the current model weights into a frozen teacher (one extra forward pass in eval mode under no_grad, on the same augmented batch, in half precision). For the remaining steps, replace the hard-label cross-entropy with 0.5 times the label-smoothed cross-entropy plus 0.5 times the KL divergence to the teacher's softmax at temperature 1. Compute the teacher logits inside the compiled forward_step, or before it. Keep the loss sum reduction, and divide by the same batch size as now so the LR scale is unchanged.
backlog.title: Self-distillation from a mid-training snapshot

backlog.spec: During training, save a copy of the model's state dict (on GPU, half precision) at 75 percent and at 90 percent of total steps, in addition to the final weights. In predict, run the three sets of weights on the input with the existing flip/shift TTA path and average their logits (or softmax probabilities) before argmax. Each snapshot is a separate model object built from the same CifarNet class, so predict must not change the live model. BatchNorm running stats come along with the state dict. This adds predict time but no training time.
backlog.title: Snapshot ensemble for prediction

backlog.spec: Add per-sample random scale augmentation to the training batch: for each image, draw a scale s uniform in [0.9, 1.1], build an affine_grid with that scale about the image centre (identity rotation, zero translation beyond the existing crop), and apply grid_sample with bilinear mode and reflection padding on the normalised batch. Do this inside a torch.compile'd helper placed after batch_crop in the loader. Keep the flip and colour jitter as they are. Predict and the whitening init use unscaled images.
backlog.title: Random scale jitter via affine grid sampling

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, replace the single fixed (a, b, c) = (3.4576, -4.7391, 2.0843) with a different triple for each of the three iterations, taken from the Polar Express minimax sequence (for example (8.2051, -22.9019, 16.4607), (4.0415, -2.9472, 0.5424), (3.8916, -2.8148, 0.5151)). Keep the target-magnitude scaling and the transpose logic unchanged. Use the three triples in order inside the unrolled loop. No other hyperparameter changes.
backlog.title: Polar Express Newton-Schulz coefficients

backlog.spec: After orthogonalisation, multiply each filter's update by max(1, rows/cols)**0.5, where rows and cols are the reshaped filter dimensions (reshaped_D and reshaped_K, before padding). This is the shape-dependent scale used in Muon variants, so that tall and wide filters get comparable update RMS. Apply it in the per-filter loop that writes final_orthogonalized_grads_list, and keep MUON_LR at its current value. Leave the rest of the optimizer unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon update RMS matching by shape

backlog.spec: Replace the Nesterov SGD optimizer1 with AdamW for the parameter groups holding the whiten bias, the norm biases and the linear head. Use betas (0.9, 0.99), eps 1e-8, and base lrs of about 1e-3 for the bias group and 2e-3 for the head, scaled by the same linear-to-zero decay that already multiplies each group. Set weight decay to WEIGHT_DECAY * BATCH_SIZE / lr to match the current decoupled decay. Keep the Muon optimizer for conv filters unchanged.
backlog.title: AdamW for head and norm biases

backlog.spec: Keep a copy of the conv filter weights (the parameters Muon updates) as slow weights, initialised from the fresh weights at the start of train(). Every 6 steps, move the slow weights toward the fast weights by 0.5 (slow += 0.5 * (fast - slow)) and copy the result back into the fast weights. Use only torch.no_grad and foreach ops, and reset the slow copies inside train() so no state carries between runs. Predict with the fast weights as before.
backlog.title: Lookahead slow weights for the conv filters

backlog.spec: Extend the progressive resolution from slot 9. For the first 40 percent of steps use 24x24 bilinear resizing, for the next 30 percent use 28x28, and for the final 30 percent use the full 32x32 images with no resize. Keep antialias=True. Pick the stage from step relative to total_train_steps inside the training loop, with no other change to the schedule, augmentation or model.
backlog.title: Three-stage resolution ramp

backlog.spec: In the training loop, for each batch draw lambda from Beta(0.2, 0.2) once per step and mix the batch with a random permutation of itself (images and one-hot labels, with the label-smoothing target built after mixing). Use a single lambda for the whole batch. Apply it only after the first 50 percent of steps, so the early phase matches the current training. Keep forward_step's loss as the summed cross entropy with the soft targets.
backlog.title: Mixup on batches with label smoothing

backlog.spec: Change the block3 width in CifarNet from 256 to 192 by setting widths['block3'] = 192. The head input becomes 192 and the head division by x.size(-1) adjusts automatically. Keep block1 and block2 unchanged. This cuts the compute of the largest layer and should move the run time down with a small accuracy cost.
backlog.title: Narrower final block

backlog.spec: Replace each nn.MaxPool2d(2) in ConvGroup with a blur-pool: a fixed 3x3 binomial low-pass filter ([1,2,1]/4 outer product, depthwise via groups=channels, stride 1 with reflect padding), followed by a stride-2 subsample, and keep max pooling after the blur. Create the filter as a buffer with the model's half dtype and channels_last layout. Leave the final MaxPool2d(3) unchanged.
backlog.title: Anti-aliased blur pooling

backlog.spec: Keep the 1536-image batch for the optimizer, but compute BatchNorm statistics over sub-batches of 256 images. Implement this in the BatchNorm module by reshaping the input from (N, C, H, W) to (N/256, 256, C, H, W) at training time and computing per-group mean and variance, while keeping the running statistics as the average over groups. Use the same momentum and eps. Predict uses running statistics as before. Keep all other code unchanged.
backlog.title: Ghost batch normalisation

backlog.spec: After the first 50 percent of steps, sample each training batch with replacement from the 50000 images, with probability proportional to the running per-example loss from the most recent epoch (stored in a float tensor of length N, initialised to ones at the start of train() and refreshed for each example seen). Compute per-example losses from the cross-entropy call with reduction='none' inside forward_step and return them along with the summed loss. Keep the number of steps and the batch size fixed, and keep the summed-loss gradient scaling so the learning rates stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Loss-weighted oversampling of hard examples

incumbent.description: Progressive resolution: the first 40 percent of training steps downsample each augmented batch to 28x28 with bilinear antialiased interpolation, then train at full 32x32, leaving the whitening init, model, schedules and predict unchanged.

memo:
Helped: only slot 9, progressive resolution (first 40 percent of steps on downsampled images). It scored -0.0252 and -0.0664, so the incumbent mean is -0.0458. It is the only compute-saving change that beat the start. The three-stage ramp (slot 16, -0.0256 in one run) was not better than the incumbent mean (+0.0202 vs incumbent), though that is within noise (sd about 0.026).

Did not help: schedule changes (trapezoid +0.4772, cosine +0.0103), the residual skip (+0.2822), cutout (+0.3046), removing the initial GELU (+0.2198), label smoothing schedule (+0.0812), Muon momentum warmup (+0.0550), and removing color jitter (+0.0468). Translation 3 (+0.0406) was also worse. The 5-view TTA (+0.0034) and head dropout (+0.0042) were neutral. Two slots crashed (learnable head scale, float32 head) and wrap-pad aborted.

Next: tune progressive resolution (low-res fraction, lower resolution), and try cheaper predict or lighter layers. Replicate the incumbent. Avoid more regularization or schedule variants, and keep edits simple.
